name: Owen Bui
role: Corroborating ham — audio engineer, technical ally
description: Vietnamese-Welsh audio engineer, licensed six years, callsign VE7OWB. Mixes for a small recording studio by trade and got into ham radio for the same reason he got into analog tape — he likes signals with texture. Gordan sends him recordings to analyze because he can hear things in a waveform that Gordan can only measure.

core_fears: Being wrong about something he's staked his professional ear on
core_desires: To find the technical explanation before anyone reaches for a non-technical one
coping_mechanisms: Runs the audio through every analysis tool he owns before he'll say a word
blind_spots: Trusts his own recall of a conversation as much as any recording, which is exactly the gap the story exploits

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Studio-technical — talks in noise floors, transients, spectral analysis
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, enthusiastic when the puzzle is purely technical; slows down and goes quiet when it stops being one
verbal_tics: Describes sounds in visual/textural terms — 'grainy,' 'clean,' 'too clean'
example_lines: The noise floor's wrong, Gordan. It's too quiet under your voice. Like the room isn't there.
speech_patterns.subtext: His professional confidence is a shield he's not aware is thin.
speech_patterns.under_pressure: Reaches for more data, more passes through the analyzer, rather than a conclusion.
speech_patterns.intimacy_register: Genuine, low-key protective of Gordan once he realizes something is actually wrong.

daily_life: Studio audio engineer; ham radio and tape collecting as parallel hobbies.

relationships.name: Gordan Rosniak
relationships.description: Analyzes Gordan's session recordings for him.

story_hooks: Finds the technical anomaly in the recordings (silence where a transmission should register)
Later repeats a private detail Gordan only ever thought at his dead mic, never transmitted — the Act 4 turn
